claims.evidence: BSE 2020 categories (letter quoting the guideline, PMC7487180): normal LVEF >=55%, borderline low 50-54%, impaired 36-49%, severely impaired <=35%. So 'above 55%' is wrong; it is 55% or more. (A local trust sheet, JPUH, prints '>55%', which leaves 55 exactly uncovered.)
claims.newSentence: The fraction of blood the left ventricle ejects each beat. Sources differ on the lower limit of normal: British Society of Echocardiography reporting categories treat 55% or more as normal (50 to 54% is borderline low), while the BHF and NHS England describe 50% or more as normal. In heart failure classification, a reduced ejection fraction is usually taken as 40% or less.

claims.evidence: NHS England 'Managing heart failure @home' glossary: ejection fraction 50% or higher is considered normal; BHF 'Understanding heart failure' booklet: normal EF is 50% and above. (BHF echo-report guide says 'over 50 to 55 per cent' and below 49 not pumping well, so the BHF is not perfectly uniform.)

NICE TA773 committee text: HFrEF trial population defined as LVEF 40% or less; ESC and NHS formulary use <=40 reduced, 41-49 mildly reduced, >=50 preserved. Note BHF booklet says 'less than 40%' and HFmrEF 40-49, a one-point discrepancy; 'usually taken as' wording covers it.

Removes the unsupported 'EF 30%' example and 'start' instruction; 'Ejection fraction well below normal: significantly reduced pumping; heart-failure treatment is considered' is plain undisputed textbook, safe wording.

Value 'above 55' disagrees with BSE (normal >=55). Source is a local trust sheet titled 'Guidance on Echocardiography Results' (not 'NHS echocardiography results guidance (based on BSE categories)'); the sheet's text reads Normal >55%, Borderline low 50-54, Impaired 36-49, Severely impaired <35 (garbled). Section label 'Ejection fraction categories' not verified.
claims.newSentence: name 'Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (British Society of Echocardiography categories)'; value '55 or more'; context 'BSE 2020 reporting categories: 50 to 54 borderline low, 36 to 49 impaired, 35 or below severely impaired'; source title 'Latest British Society of Echocardiography recommendations for left ventricular ejection fraction categorisation (Heart/BMJ letter, PMC)', url https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7487180/, section 'Categories'. Keep the JPUH PDF only as a secondary reference with its true title.

claims.evidence: NHS England page excerpt: ejection fraction measured as a percentage; 50% or higher considered normal; you can have a normal ejection fraction and still have heart failure (HFpEF). Title and URL match; section 'Ejection fraction' = glossary entry, reasonable.

Retrieved text of the NHS England HFpEF pathway support tool gives EF >=50% for HFpEF and says HFmrEF should be treated as HFrEF for scope; no '40 or less' and no 'Coding table' section was retrieved from that page (a regional NHS England North West PDF does use a separate HFmrEF code for 41-49). The value 40 or less itself is supported by NICE TA773 and ESC.

Remove the pathway-tool URL from this record (it may stay as a reference only for the 50 or more preserved/HFmrEF-as-HFrEF scope point).

notes: (e) BSE normal is >=55 (not above 55); BHF/NHS England 50 or more normal confirmed; HFrEF <=40 confirmed from NICE/ESC but NOT from the NHS England pathway tool excerpt; BHF booklet says <40. Local JPUH sheet is a single trust document: weak as a UK reference.
